findings.issue_text: Broken authorization logic: `&&` instead of `||` in isTeamAdminOrOwner check means a user must be both team admin and team owner to pass, making the feature unavailable to team admins/owners
Duplicate emails in guests input are not rejected server-side, causing Prisma createMany unique-constraint failure and an opaque 500 error
Email send failures in sendAddGuestsEmails are silently swallowed with only a bare console.log, masking partial success as full success
Blacklist comparison is case-inconsistent: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased but guest emails are not, so case variants bypass the blacklist and the 'already attendee' filter
EventManager is constructed with the actor's credentials (ctx.user) rather than the organizer's, so attendee-triggered updates may run against the wrong calendar
Client validation error flag setIsInvalidEmail(true) is never cleared after a successful retry, leaving the red warning visible during the success toast
Empty-input Add click shows a misleading 'Emails must be unique and valid' error because initial state [""] bypasses the length check but fails email validation
OrganizerAddGuestsEmail subject indexes attendees[0].name without guarding for an empty attendees array, which would throw
newGuests.includes(attendee.email) uses exact case matching, so guests added with different casing receive the wrong notification email/ICS
Team admin check uses && instead of ||, requiring caller to be both admin AND owner, so plain admins are denied in addGuests.handler.ts:50-53
Blacklisted guest email comparison is case-sensitive, allowing bypass via different casing in addGuests.handler.ts:76-84
Any booking attendee can add arbitrary unlimited guests to someone else's booking, exposing event details and turning attendees into a distribution channel in addGuests.handler.ts:55-62
No cap on guest array size and no case-insensitive deduplication against existing attendees, enabling mass emails/calendar writes and duplicate attendee records in addGuests.handler.ts:71-101
EventManager constructed with ctx.user credentials instead of booking organizer's, so calendar attendee updates fail for non-organizer callers in addGuests.handler.ts:157-166
findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId || 0 throws unhandled Prisma error (500) for bookings without a userId in addGuests.handler.ts:64-72
addGuests schema has no .max() on the guests array, allowing unbounded DB writes and email fan-out (email-bombing vector); cap the array and total attendees
newGuests.includes(attendee.email) in email-manager.ts:540 causes O(attendees × newGuests) membership checks inside the email fan-out loop; should use a Set
Email classification comparison is case-sensitive while emails are user input, so the same guest with different casing receives the wrong email template; should be case-insensitive
utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate() in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:49 invalidates the entire bookings router instead of the specific affected query, causing redundant refetches; use scoped invalidation
isTeamAdminOrOwner in addGuests.handler.ts:66-68 uses && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner so a mere admin fails both branches; likely intended ||
isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, so only users who are both team admin and owner pass; team admins get FORBIDDEN
?? 0 sentinel relies on isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner tolerating nonexistent teamId 0; may throw for personal bookings
Server input schema doesn't enforce guest uniqueness; duplicates in the guests array create duplicate Attendee rows and double emails
uniqueGuests only dedupes against existing attendees, not within the guests array itself
Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive since guests are compared raw against lowercased blacklisted emails, allowing case-evasion (A@x.com bypasses blacklist)
Existing-attendee dedup check is case-sensitive, allowing A@x.com to evade dedup against a@x.com attendees
No email normalization (.toLowerCase()) in boundary schema or handler
sendAddGuestsEmails new-guest matching (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) is case-sensitive, causing new guests to receive the wrong email (notification instead of full ICS invite)
Mutation returns hardcoded English { message: 'Guests added' } instead of an untranslated code; UI does its own t()
Response carries no structured data (e.g., added attendee list) for callers to reconcile with silently dropped guests from dedup/blacklist filtering
EventManager is built from ctx.user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so updateCalendarAttendees fails or mutates the wrong account's event for attendee-triggered adds
Dynamic bookings (eventType: null) not handled: isTeamAdmin(user.id, 0) behavior and seatsPerTimeSlot: undefined make the contract undefined/untested for these bookings
UI exposes the add-guests action for every booking via BookingListItem without gating for dynamic bookings
Calendar update failure (updateCalendarAttendees throwing) leaves attendees persisted with no rollback/compensation and dedupe filter prevents retry of missing calendar update/emails
Authorization bug: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, denying team admins who are not owners
Unhandled prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow with booking.userId || 0 causes raw 500 for bookings with null userId instead of proper TRPC error
Email send failure silently swallowed with console.log, discarding error object with no observability while API returns success
Case-sensitivity gaps: guest emails not lowercased so blacklist and attendee dedupe checks can be bypassed, producing duplicate attendees
EventManager built with acting user's credentials instead of organizer's, causing calendar update failure when non-organizer adds guests
No server-side duplicate-submit protection; non-idempotent createMany allows double-tap/two-tab duplicate inserts; consider unique constraint on (bookingId, email)
isInvalidEmail error state never cleared when user edits emails, causing stale error banner and conflating server/client errors
Authorization logic uses && instead of || in isTeamAdminOrOwner, denying access to team admins/owners who aren't the booking organizer
Blacklist bypass via case sensitivity: guest emails aren't lowercased/normalized before blacklist and duplicate-attendee checks
Server-side schema doesn't dedupe the guest list, allowing duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails when mutation is called directly
Client-side schema re-declares ZAddGuestsInputSchema inline instead of importing the shared server schema, risking validation drift
Calendar update uses the calling user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials, potentially updating the wrong calendar or failing
Email failure silently swallowed: error logged without details and caller receives success response even if emails fail
No seat-capacity check when adding guests to seated event types, allowing guests beyond the configured limit
Guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings since there's no booking.status check in handler or UI action
Blacklist guest email check is case-sensitive, allowing uppercase-variant emails to bypass the blacklist
Duplicate-attendee check is case-sensitive, allowing case-variant emails to create duplicate attendees and calendar/ics entries
Email send failures are swallowed with console.log and the handler still returns 'Guests added', so UI reports success while guests were never notified
Client clears entered emails on success even when emails failed to send, so the guest list cannot be recovered
DB write succeeds before calendar update with no transaction/rollback, so a calendar failure leaves guests persisted but mutation reports failure
Retry path is broken: re-running the handler hits empty-guests BAD_REQUEST since guests already exist, preventing re-notification
No booking status check, allowing guests to be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings
ics attachment sent with status CONFIRMED and method REQUEST, re-confirming cancelled meetings in attendees' calendars
No check for past bookings, so attendees receive fresh REQUEST ics for events already over
seatsPerTimeSlot capacity is never enforced, allowing unlimited guests beyond seated-event capacity
Authorization uses && so user must be both team admin AND owner, likely locking out owners
isAttendee grants add-guest rights to any attendee while the booker (booking.email) is not checked, an inverted/incomplete authorization intent
Calendar event is updated using the requesting user's credentials instead of the organizer's, causing failures or divergent state when an attendee triggers the flow
isInvalidEmail warning never resets when the user edits input, persisting until Cancel
Server silently dedupes already-attendee emails and reports 'Guests added' success even when nothing was added
findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId || 0 for team bookings throws an unhandled Prisma record-not-found as a raw 500 instead of a clean TRPC error

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate emails in guests input are not rejected server-side, causing Prisma createMany unique-constraint failure and an opaque 500 error
Email send failures in sendAddGuestsEmails are silently swallowed with only a bare console.log, masking partial success as full success

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the call to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and then continues to return `{ message: "Guests added" }` (success) regardless of whether sending emails failed. The error object isn’t logged or surfaced, so an email send failure (including partial failures from `Promise.all` inside `sendAddGuestsEmails`) is silently swallowed and masked as full success to the caller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist comparison is case-inconsistent: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased but guest emails are not, so case variants bypass the blacklist and the 'already attendee' filter
EventManager is constructed with the actor's credentials (ctx.user) rather than the organizer's, so attendee-triggered updates may run against the wrong calendar

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation allows execution by an attendee (`isAttendee` check). However, the calendar update is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`, where `user` is `ctx.user` (the actor), not the booking organizer. The booking organizer and their credentials are available (`booking.user.credentials` is included in the initial `findFirst`), but unused. Therefore, when an attendee triggers this mutation, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run using the attendee’s credentials, which is a verifiable correctness issue consistent with the proposed finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client validation error flag setIsInvalidEmail(true) is never cleared after a successful retry, leaving the red warning visible during the success toast

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on failed client-side validation in `handleAdd`, but it is only reset in the Cancel button handler. On a subsequent successful add (`addGuestsMutation.onSuccess`), the code closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`, but never calls `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`. Since the dialog component stays mounted (it’s always rendered in `BookingListItem` and controlled via `open`), reopening the dialog after a successful add can still show the red warning even though the last action succeeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Empty-input Add click shows a misleading 'Emails must be unique and valid' error because initial state [""] bypasses the length check but fails email validation
matched_golden_ids: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same root problem: initializing the emails array as [""] causes validation/UX issues because the empty string participates in checks (bypassing length-based logic and failing email validation). The golden comment also suggests starting with [] and handling empty state, but the candidate still identifies the same underlying issue with the initial [""] state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OrganizerAddGuestsEmail subject indexes attendees[0].name without guarding for an empty attendees array, which would throw

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the email subject is built using `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. If `this.calEvent.attendees` is an empty array, `this.calEvent.attendees[0]` is `undefined` and accessing `.name` will throw at runtime. There is no guard or fallback in this diff to ensure `attendees[0]` exists before dereferencing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: newGuests.includes(attendee.email) uses exact case matching, so guests added with different casing receive the wrong notification email/ICS

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)`, the code decides which email template to send using `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))`, which is a case-sensitive string comparison. In the new add-guests flow, neither the frontend nor backend normalizes emails to a consistent casing (the zod schemas allow mixed-case emails, and the handler stores `email: guest` as provided). As a result, if the same logical email appears with different casing between `newGuests` and `calendarEvent.attendees[*].email` (e.g., due to prior storage/normalization elsewhere), the attendee can be misclassified as “new” vs “existing” and receive the wrong notification/ICS. This is a correctness issue introduced by the diff’s case-sensitive membership check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Team admin check uses && instead of ||, requiring caller to be both admin AND owner, so plain admins are denied in addGuests.handler.ts:50-53

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code defines `isTeamAdminOrOwner` as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which will only be true if the user is both a team admin and a team owner. That contradicts the variable name and the intended permission logic implied by it, and it means a user who is an admin but not an owner (or vice versa) will fail the permission check and be denied (`FORBIDDEN`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklisted guest email comparison is case-sensitive, allowing bypass via different casing in addGuests.handler.ts:76-84
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same flaw: the blacklist email check is case-sensitive because the blacklist is lowercased but the incoming guest email isn’t normalized, allowing bypass by changing email casing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Any booking attendee can add arbitrary unlimited guests to someone else's booking, exposing event details and turning attendees into a distribution channel in addGuests.handler.ts:55-62

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation explicitly authorizes any user who is already an attendee of the booking (`const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and then `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`). Once authorized, it will create new attendee records for whatever emails are provided (minus existing attendees and a blacklist) and then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which can send full event/calendar details to those addresses. There is no server-side cap on number of `guests` (only `z.array(z.string().email())`), so an attendee can add an arbitrary number of guests to a booking they don’t organize, effectively using the system to distribute invites/event details.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No cap on guest array size and no case-insensitive deduplication against existing attendees, enabling mass emails/calendar writes and duplicate attendee records in addGuests.handler.ts:71-101

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the input schema allows an unbounded `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)`, so a caller can submit a very large list, causing potentially expensive DB `createMany`, calendar attendee updates, and email sends. Also, the deduplication against existing attendees is case-sensitive: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and blacklist check lowercases only the blacklist values, not the incoming `guest`. This allows duplicates like `Test@x.com` vs `test@x.com` to bypass filtering and be inserted/sent. These issues are directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager constructed with ctx.user credentials instead of booking organizer's, so calendar attendee updates fail for non-organizer callers in addGuests.handler.ts:157-166

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the booking’s organizer is fetched (booking.userId) and the booking query even includes booking.user.credentials, but the calendar update uses `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and constructs `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` where `user` is `ctx.user` (the caller). For callers who are not the organizer (e.g., team admin/owner or an attendee allowed by the permission check), this will use the wrong account’s calendar credentials when calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, making external calendar updates likely to fail or update the wrong calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId || 0 throws unhandled Prisma error (500) for bookings without a userId in addGuests.handler.ts:64-72

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the organizer is loaded with `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. The `|| 0` indicates `booking.userId` may be null/undefined. If it is, the query becomes `id: 0`, which will not exist and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma error. This throw is not converted to a `TRPCError` (unlike the earlier booking-not-found check), so it will bubble up as an internal error (500) instead of a controlled/expected error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests schema has no .max() on the guests array, allowing unbounded DB writes and email fan-out (email-bombing vector); cap the array and total attendees

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests` is defined as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()` or other bound. The handler then does `attendees.createMany({ data: guestsFullDetails })`, so a caller can trigger an unbounded number of attendee rows to be inserted in one request (subject only to DB/prisma limits not shown here). It also triggers email fan-out: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` ultimately maps over `calendarEvent.attendees` and sends an email per attendee (plus organizer/team-member emails) with `Promise.all`, so a large guests list can cause a large burst of outbound emails. There is no cap on total attendees either; it only filters duplicates vs existing attendees and blacklisted emails, which doesn't prevent large unique inputs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: newGuests.includes(attendee.email) in email-manager.ts:540 causes O(attendees × newGuests) membership checks inside the email fan-out loop; should use a Set

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a nested membership check: in sendAddGuestsEmails(), it iterates over calendarEvent.attendees and calls newGuests.includes(attendee.email) inside the map, which is O(attendees × newGuests) in the worst case. However, this is a performance micro-optimization rather than a clear defect/bug/security/correctness issue demonstrated by the diff; there’s no evidence here that attendee/guest lists are large enough for this to be problematic, and the logic remains correct.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email classification comparison is case-sensitive while emails are user input, so the same guest with different casing receives the wrong email template; should be case-insensitive

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the code classifies attendees using `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))`, which is a case-sensitive string comparison. `newGuests` comes from user input (`guests` passed from the client) and is not normalized to lowercase anywhere in the diff. Likewise, the server-side duplicate filter uses `guest === attendee.email` (also case-sensitive). Therefore, if an attendee email already exists as `foo@bar.com` and the user adds `Foo@bar.com`, the code will treat it as different: it may add a duplicate attendee record and, regardless, the existing attendee will not match `includes(...)` and will receive the "added guests" template instead of the intended "scheduled" template for newly added guests. This is a real correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate() in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:49 invalidates the entire bookings router instead of the specific affected query, causing redundant refetches; use scoped invalidation

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog` the code calls `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()` after a successful mutation, which will invalidate all cached queries under the `viewer.bookings` router. That may cause broader refetching than strictly necessary, but it is still correct behavior and can be intentional to keep any bookings-related views consistent (list, detail, attendees, etc.). The diff does not show a more specific query that must be targeted, nor does it demonstrate an actual bug or incorrectness—this is a performance optimization suggestion, not a verifiable defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner in addGuests.handler.ts:66-68 uses && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner so a mere admin fails both branches; likely intended ||

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts the variable is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, but it is computed with `&&` between `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)`. That requires the user to be both an admin and an owner to pass the team-privileged branch. As a result, a user who is only a team admin (not an owner) will have `isTeamAdminOrOwner === false` and will be forbidden unless they are also the organizer or an attendee. This is a concrete logic defect visible in the diff and is very likely intended to be `||` (admin OR owner).

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, so only users who are both team admin and owner pass; team admins get FORBIDDEN

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. That requires the user to be BOTH a team admin and a team owner to satisfy `isTeamAdminOrOwner`. The subsequent permission check denies access when `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee`, so a user who is a team admin but not an owner (a common case) will fail `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and be incorrectly rejected with `FORBIDDEN` unless they also happen to be the organizer or an attendee. This is a concrete logic bug introduced/present in the diff; it likely should be `||` (or separate checks) to match the intent of the variable name.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ?? 0 sentinel relies on isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner tolerating nonexistent teamId 0; may throw for personal bookings

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code does pass a fallback teamId of 0 into isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner when booking.eventType?.teamId is null/undefined. However, the diff provides no evidence that these helper functions throw or misbehave on teamId=0 (they may simply return false). Claiming it “may throw for personal bookings” depends on behavior outside the diff and isn’t verifiable from the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server input schema doesn't enforce guest uniqueness; duplicates in the guests array create duplicate Attendee rows and double emails
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe that the guests input is not deduplicated for repeated emails, so createMany can insert duplicate Attendee rows (and trigger duplicate emails).

adjudication_records.issue_text: uniqueGuests only dedupes against existing attendees, not within the guests array itself

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` is computed with `guests.filter(...)` only excluding emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails. There is no deduplication of duplicates within the incoming `guests` array itself, and the server-side Zod schema (`ZAddGuestsInputSchema`) also does not enforce uniqueness. Therefore a caller can send duplicate emails and they will remain in `uniqueGuests`, potentially causing duplicate attendee rows (or a DB error if there’s a uniqueness constraint) and is a real correctness issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive since guests are compared raw against lowercased blacklisted emails, allowing case-evasion (A@x.com bypasses blacklist)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is derived as lowercase strings (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the filter checks `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` using the raw `guest` value without normalizing case. This makes the blacklist check effectively case-sensitive and allows bypass via different casing (e.g., `A@x.com` when `a@x.com` is blacklisted).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Existing-attendee dedup check is case-sensitive, allowing A@x.com to evade dedup against a@x.com attendees

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the existing-attendee deduplication uses strict equality (`guest === attendee.email`) when filtering `uniqueGuests`, and `guest` is not normalized (e.g., lowercased) before comparison. This allows adding `A@x.com` even if an attendee already exists as `a@x.com`, since the check is case-sensitive. The client-side uniqueness check in `AddGuestsDialog` (`new Set(emails)`) is also case-sensitive, reinforcing the issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No email normalization (.toLowerCase()) in boundary schema or handler

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `z.string().email()` and the handler (`addGuestsHandler`) compares raw `guest` strings against `attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails` without normalizing case. The blacklist is lowercased (`.toLowerCase()`), but incoming `guests` are not, so `Test@Example.com` would not match a blacklisted `test@example.com`. Similarly, duplicates can slip through if an existing attendee email differs only by case, because the filter uses `guest === attendee.email`. No `.toLowerCase()` (or other normalization) is applied at the boundary or before these comparisons/mutations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails new-guest matching (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) is case-sensitive, causing new guests to receive the wrong email (notification instead of full ICS invite)

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the branch is `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide which template to send. However, in the same diff the new attendee records are created directly from the input emails (`uniqueGuests` comes from `guests` without case normalization, and `guestsFullDetails.email` is set to that same string). The `CalendarEvent.attendees` list is then built from those persisted attendee emails, so for newly added guests `attendee.email` will match the corresponding string in `newGuests` exactly. A case-sensitivity mismatch would require some other layer (not shown in this diff) to normalize email casing (e.g., lowercasing on write), which is speculative and not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mutation returns hardcoded English { message: 'Guests added' } instead of an untranslated code; UI does its own t()

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a hardcoded English return value in `addGuests.handler.ts` (`return { message: "Guests added" };`). However, in the same diff the UI (`AddGuestsDialog`) does not consume this message at all; it shows a toast using its own i18n key (`showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")`). There is no evidence in the diff of a contract requiring server responses to return translation keys instead of English strings, nor any functional issue caused by this return value. At most this is an API consistency/style preference, not a clear defect verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Response carries no structured data (e.g., added attendee list) for callers to reconcile with silently dropped guests from dedup/blacklist filtering

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server filters the requested `guests` into `uniqueGuests` by removing emails already in `booking.attendees` and emails in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. If `uniqueGuests` is non-empty, it proceeds to add only `uniqueGuests` via `createMany`, but the mutation response is always `return { message: "Guests added" }` with no data about which emails were added vs ignored. This means callers (e.g., the new `AddGuestsDialog`) cannot reconcile partial success when some requested guests were silently dropped by dedup/blacklist filtering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is built from ctx.user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so updateCalendarAttendees fails or mutates the wrong account's event for attendee-triggered adds

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the mutation explicitly allows non-organizers (team admin/owner or even an attendee) to call addGuests. However, the calendar update is performed by constructing EventManager with `...user` where `user` is `ctx.user` (the caller) and `credentials` are fetched via `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. The booking organizer is fetched separately (`organizer` from `booking.userId`) but their credentials are never used. If an attendee triggers this, `updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run with the attendee's integrations instead of the organizer's, which can fail to update the organizer's calendar event or affect the wrong connected account. This mismatch is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dynamic bookings (eventType: null) not handled: isTeamAdmin(user.id, 0) behavior and seatsPerTimeSlot: undefined make the contract undefined/untested for these bookings

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s new addGuests handler consistently guards `booking.eventType` access with optional chaining (e.g., `booking.eventType?.teamId`, `booking.eventType?.recurringEvent`, `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`). For `eventType: null`, the team checks receive `0` via `?? 0`, but the code does not rely on those checks being true to function; it falls back to `isOrganizer` / `isAttendee` permission paths, so dynamic bookings are still handled. The claim that `isTeamAdmin(user.id, 0)` has “undefined behavior” and that `seatsPerTimeSlot: undefined` breaks a “contract” is speculative and not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UI exposes the add-guests action for every booking via BookingListItem without gating for dynamic bookings

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an "add_members" action unconditionally to `bookingActions` in `BookingListItem`, so it will appear for all bookings rendered by that component. However, the proposed finding’s specific claim about needing gating for “dynamic bookings” is not verifiable from the diff: there is no reference to “dynamic bookings” or any existing gating pattern/flag being bypassed. Additionally, permission enforcement is handled server-side in `addGuestsHandler` (it rejects unauthorized users), so this is not a clear correctness/security defect introduced by the diff—at most it could be a product/UI decision not evidenced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update failure (updateCalendarAttendees throwing) leaves attendees persisted with no rollback/compensation and dedupe filter prevents retry of missing calendar update/emails

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code persists new attendees first via prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...) and only afterwards calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) without any try/catch or transaction. If updateCalendarAttendees throws, the mutation will error while the DB write has already happened, leaving attendees persisted with no rollback/compensation. Additionally, retries with the same guest emails are blocked by the later dedupe logic: uniqueGuests filters out emails already present in booking.attendees and if uniqueGuests.length === 0 it throws BAD_REQUEST, so a user cannot re-run the mutation to re-attempt the failed calendar update/email sending for those guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization bug: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, denying team admins who are not owners

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, permission is computed as `isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. The variable name and intended semantics (“admin OR owner”) imply this should be `||`. As written, a team admin who is not also an owner (or an owner who is not also an admin) will fail `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and be denied unless they happen to also be the organizer/attendee. This is a concrete authorization logic defect introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhandled prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow with booking.userId || 0 causes raw 500 for bookings with null userId instead of proper TRPC error

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is fetched with `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null/undefined` (the code explicitly guards with `|| 0`, implying it can be), this will query `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw. That thrown error is not wrapped/converted into a `TRPCError`, so it will surface as an internal error (500/INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR) rather than a deliberate, user-facing TRPC error like NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failure silently swallowed with console.log, discarding error object with no observability while API returns success
Case-sensitivity gaps: guest emails not lowercased so blacklist and attendee dedupe checks can be bypassed, producing duplicate attendees

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, both the attendee dedupe and blacklist checks are case-sensitive: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. However, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is explicitly lowercased while `guest` is not, so an input like `Bad@Example.com` will not match a blacklist entry `bad@example.com`. Similarly, an existing attendee `alice@example.com` can be duplicated by adding `Alice@Example.com` because the equality check is exact string match. Neither the TRPC schema nor the UI normalizes emails to lowercase, so this bypass is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager built with acting user's credentials instead of organizer's, causing calendar update failure when non-organizer adds guests

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is the acting session user (could be a team admin/owner or an attendee per the permission checks). However, the booking’s organizer is `booking.userId` and is fetched separately as `organizer`, and the booking query even includes `booking.user.credentials`, but those organizer credentials are not used. If a non-organizer adds guests, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run with the non-organizer’s credentials, which can reasonably cause failure or update the wrong calendar since the integration typically belongs to the organizer/booking owner.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No server-side duplicate-submit protection; non-idempotent createMany allows double-tap/two-tab duplicate inserts; consider unique constraint on (bookingId, email)

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` performs a read (`findFirst` incl. attendees) then a write (`booking.update` with `attendees.createMany`) without any server-side idempotency/uniqueness enforcement. It filters out emails already present in `booking.attendees`, but (1) it does not de-duplicate emails within the incoming `guests` array on the server, and (2) concurrent requests can both observe the same pre-state and both run `createMany`, allowing duplicate attendee rows unless there is a DB unique constraint or `createMany({ skipDuplicates: true })`/transactional protection (none shown/used in the diff). The client has a uniqueness refine, but that can be bypassed; server schema only validates email format.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail error state never cleared when user edits emails, causing stale error banner and conflating server/client errors

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails in `handleAdd()`. However, it is only cleared on the Cancel button click (`setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). Editing emails via `MultiEmail` only calls `setMultiEmailValue` and never resets `isInvalidEmail`, so the error banner can remain visible even after the user fixes the input and retries. This is a verifiable stale UI/error-state bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization logic uses && instead of || in isTeamAdminOrOwner, denying access to team admins/owners who aren't the booking organizer

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

This requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass the later permission check:

```ts
if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;
```

So a user who is a team admin (but not owner) or a team owner (but not admin) will be denied unless they are also the booking organizer or an attendee. That matches the finding and is a real authorization/correctness bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist bypass via case sensitivity: guest emails aren't lowercased/normalized before blacklist and duplicate-attendee checks

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the blacklist is normalized to lowercase (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but incoming `guests` are compared without normalization: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` and duplicates are checked via `guest === attendee.email`. Since both checks are case-sensitive, a blacklisted email like `bad@ex.com` can be bypassed by submitting `Bad@ex.com`, and an existing attendee `user@ex.com` won’t be detected if the input is `User@ex.com` (or vice versa). The Zod `.email()` validation does not enforce lowercase, so this is a real, verifiable correctness/security issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server-side schema doesn't dedupe the guest list, allowing duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails when mutation is called directly

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness. In `addGuestsHandler`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails, but it does not dedupe duplicates within the provided `guests` array itself. As a result, calling the mutation directly with `guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"]` will produce `guestsFullDetails` with duplicates and attempt `attendees.createMany` with duplicate rows (and `createMany` is not configured with `skipDuplicates`). Client-side UI has a uniqueness refinement, but the server does not, so the issue is real when bypassing the UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side schema re-declares ZAddGuestsInputSchema inline instead of importing the shared server schema, risking validation drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the client dialog defining its own Zod schema inline (`z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)`) instead of importing `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` added on the server (`{ bookingId: z.number(), guests: z.array(z.string().email()) }`). However, this is not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff: the client schema is intentionally only validating the email list (and additionally enforces uniqueness), while the server validates the full input via tRPC and also performs its own filtering/validation in the handler. The claimed “validation drift” is a maintainability concern and speculative (depends on future schema changes), not a concrete bug/correctness issue evidenced in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update uses the calling user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials, potentially updating the wrong calendar or failing

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code constructs `EventManager` using the authenticated caller (`const { user } = ctx`) and their credentials (`const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); ... new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`). However, the mutation explicitly allows non-organizers to call it (`isAttendee` or team admin/owner). In those cases, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will attempt calendar updates using the caller’s credentials rather than the booking organizer’s credentials, which can update the wrong calendar or fail due to lack of access. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email failure silently swallowed: error logged without details and caller receives success response even if emails fail
No seat-capacity check when adding guests to seated event types, allowing guests beyond the configured limit

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` unconditionally appends new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` after only filtering out existing attendees/blacklisted emails. There is no check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (or any existing attendee count) before creating more attendees. Since the diff explicitly carries `seatsPerTimeSlot` into the constructed `CalendarEvent` (suggesting seat-capacity is a real concept for this booking), this mutation can add guests beyond the configured seat limit for seated event types.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings since there's no booking.status check in handler or UI action

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` fetches the booking by `id` only and does not check any booking lifecycle/status field (e.g., cancelled/rejected) before updating attendees (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`) and sending update emails. On the UI side, the new action `{ id: "add_members", ... }` is added to `actions` without any conditional gating based on booking state, so the dialog/mutation can be triggered regardless of whether the booking is cancelled/rejected. If the product expects cancelled/rejected bookings to be immutable, this diff introduces a real correctness/authorization gap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist guest email check is case-sensitive, allowing uppercase-variant emails to bypass the blacklist

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS are normalized to lowercase (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the incoming `guest` values are compared without normalization: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `guest` is not lowercased (and emails can contain uppercase characters), an uppercase-variant like `Blocked@Example.com` would not match `blocked@example.com` in the blacklist, allowing bypass. This is a real, verifiable case-sensitivity bug introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-attendee check is case-sensitive, allowing case-variant emails to create duplicate attendees and calendar/ics entries

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the duplicate filtering uses a case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. Neither `guest` nor `attendee.email` is normalized (e.g., `toLowerCase()`), so an existing attendee `test@example.com` would not block adding `Test@Example.com`, creating duplicate attendee rows and triggering calendar/ICS updates/emails for effectively the same address. The client-side uniqueness check in `AddGuestsDialog` (`new Set(emails)`) is also case-sensitive, so it won’t prevent case-variant duplicates either.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failures are swallowed with console.log and the handler still returns 'Guests added', so UI reports success while guests were never notified

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email notification step is wrapped in a `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch { console.log(...) }` block and the error is not rethrown. The handler then still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so the TRPC mutation resolves successfully even if email sending fails. In the UI (`AddGuestsDialog`), `onSuccess` always shows `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")` and closes the dialog, meaning the UI will indicate success despite guests potentially not being notified due to the swallowed email error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client clears entered emails on success even when emails failed to send, so the guest list cannot be recovered
DB write succeeds before calendar update with no transaction/rollback, so a calendar failure leaves guests persisted but mutation reports failure

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the DB is updated first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards it calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. There is no surrounding transaction or compensating rollback. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (calendar API/credentials/network failure), the tRPC mutation will error/return failure, but the attendee rows have already been persisted in the DB, leaving state inconsistent with the calendar and user-visible failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Retry path is broken: re-running the handler hits empty-guests BAD_REQUEST since guests already exist, preventing re-notification
No booking status check, allowing guests to be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler`, the booking is fetched by `id` and then updated (`prisma.booking.update` with `attendees.createMany`) without any check of a booking status/state (e.g., CANCELLED/REJECTED). Nothing in this diff prevents calling `viewer.bookings.addGuests` for a cancelled/rejected booking as long as the caller passes the permission check, so guests can be added regardless of booking state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ics attachment sent with status CONFIRMED and method REQUEST, re-confirming cancelled meetings in attendees' calendars

adjudication.rationale: The new add-guests email templates attach an ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` (see `packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`). The new `addGuestsHandler` (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`) fetches and updates a booking by id but does not check any booking status (e.g., cancelled) before sending these emails. If this mutation is invoked for a cancelled booking, recipients could receive an iCalendar REQUEST marking the event as CONFIRMED, which can re-add/reconfirm a previously cancelled event in some calendar clients. That mismatch between booking state and ICS state is a concrete correctness risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No check for past bookings, so attendees receive fresh REQUEST ics for events already over

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` flow sends calendar update emails (with `method: "REQUEST"` in both `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`) unconditionally. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is fetched and updated, then `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` are called without any check that `booking.startTime/endTime` are in the future. The UI also adds the action menu item without any condition. So a past booking can be modified and will trigger fresh REQUEST .ics emails for an already-finished event.

adjudication_records.issue_text: seatsPerTimeSlot capacity is never enforced, allowing unlimited guests beyond seated-event capacity

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` appends attendees to an existing booking via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` without checking `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (or any other capacity field) against the current attendee count + new guests. Although `evt` includes `seatsPerTimeSlot`, it is only passed to calendar/email logic and does not enforce limits. This makes it possible to add guests beyond seated-event capacity for event types that use `seatsPerTimeSlot`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization uses && so user must be both team admin AND owner, likely locking out owners

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the authorization flag `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

This requires the user to be BOTH a team admin AND a team owner to pass that check. Given the variable name and typical intent (“admin OR owner”), this will incorrectly deny access to users who are only admins or only owners (depending on how those predicates are defined), making the finding a real, verifiable logic/authorization issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isAttendee grants add-guest rights to any attendee while the booker (booking.email) is not checked, an inverted/incomplete authorization intent

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, authorization allows the mutation if `isAttendee` is true: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and then `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`. This means any user whose email matches any attendee on the booking (including non-booking guests, if they have an account) can add more guests. There is no check restricting this to the original booker/primary attendee versus other attendees/guests, so the finding that attendee-level access is overly broad is supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar event is updated using the requesting user's credentials instead of the organizer's, causing failures or divergent state when an attendee triggers the flow

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the flow explicitly allows an attendee to trigger the mutation (`const isAttendee = ...` and the permission check allows `isAttendee`). However, the calendar update is performed via `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` where `user` and `credentials` come from `ctx.user` (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`), i.e., the requesting user. That means when an attendee triggers “add guests”, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run with the attendee’s credentials rather than the organizer’s (or booking owner’s) credentials, which can reasonably cause calendar update failures or inconsistent state compared to the organizer’s calendar. The diff does not show any switch to organizer/booking user credentials for this operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail warning never resets when the user edits input, persisting until Cancel

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails in `handleAdd()`. However, `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` is only called in the Cancel button handler. The `MultiEmail` inputs update `multiEmailValue` via `setMultiEmailValue`, but no code clears `isInvalidEmail` on input change. As a result, once the warning appears it will continue to render even after the user corrects the emails, until they hit Cancel (and it also isn’t reset on `onSuccess`, so it can persist across reopening the dialog).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server silently dedupes already-attendee emails and reports 'Guests added' success even when nothing was added

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server filters out emails that are already attendees (and blacklisted) into `uniqueGuests`, but it explicitly checks `if (uniqueGuests.length === 0) throw new TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" });`. So it will NOT return success when nothing new was added; it errors instead. While it does ignore already-attendee emails when there are other new guests, the specific claim that it “reports 'Guests added' success even when nothing was added” is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId || 0 for team bookings throws an unhandled Prisma record-not-found as a raw 500 instead of a clean TRPC error

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is fetched via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. This explicitly anticipates `booking.userId` being falsy (null/undefined) and substitutes `0`, which will not match any real user. `findFirstOrThrow` will then throw a Prisma not-found error, and this handler does not catch/translate it into a `TRPCError`, so it will propagate as an internal server error (500) rather than a controlled TRPC error response. While the finding’s “team bookings” condition isn’t proven in the diff, the unhandled throw path is present and verifiable.
